title: Gabber roots construct an integral idempotent section factor
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, B an etale A-algebra [def-weil-etale-morphism], and I an ideal of A contained in its Jacobson radical. Assume every monic polynomial X^n(X-1)+sum_{j=0}^n a_j X^j with n>=1 and all a_j in I has a root alpha in 1+I. Given an A-algebra map sigma:B->A/I, there is an idempotent e in B such that A->B[1/e] is integral, the induced structure map A/I->B[1/e]/IB[1/e] is bijective, and there is an A-algebra map rho:B[1/e]->A/I with rho(x/1)=sigma(x) for every x in B. This asserts the integral factor construction, not an isomorphism A->B[1/e].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), implication (5)$\Rightarrow$(2) and its proof (paragraphs from 'Assume (5). We will show that (2) holds' to the end of the proof): the section gives $A'/IA'\cong A/I\times C$ (Algebra Lemmas 00U7 lemma-map-between-etale and 00U8 lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented); integral closure $B'$ of $A$ in $A'$ and Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type, line 2502); a finite subalgebra $B''$ and Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290) give $f$ as in (b) with $f(b)=0$; the root $a\in1+I$ splits $A[T]/(f)$ and hence $B'$ and $A'$; Lemma Tag 0ELZ (lemma-check-isomorphism-zariski, line 2265) concludes

proof.text: *Notation; the decomposition modulo $I$.* Fix $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale and the $A$-algebra map $\sigma:A'\to A/I$; write $\bar A'=A'/IA'=(A/I)\otimes_AA'$ and $\pi:A\to A/I$. Since $\sigma(IA')=\pi(I)\sigma(A')=0$, $\sigma$ factors as $A'\to\bar A'\xrightarrow{\bar\sigma}A/I$, with $\bar\sigma$ a homomorphism of $A/I$-algebras. $\operatorname{Spec}\bar A'\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] (with $R=A/I$, $S=\bar A'$, $s=\bar\sigma$) there is an idempotent $\varepsilon\in\bar A'$ with $\bar\sigma(\varepsilon)=1$, $\ker\bar\sigma=(1-\varepsilon)\bar A'$, so $\bar A'\cong A/I\times C$ with $C=(1-\varepsilon)\bar A'$ and $\bar\sigma$ the first projection, and $\bar\sigma$ induces an isomorphism of $A/I$-algebras $\psi:\bar A'_\varepsilon\xrightarrow{\sim}A/I$. In particular $C_1:=\varepsilon\bar A'\cong A/I$ is finite over $A/I$. (Stacks: equation (GCHP), via Algebra 00U7 and 00U8.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), first paragraph ('the section $\sigma$ determines a decomposition $A'/IA'\cong A/I\times C$')

proof.text: *The integral closure (Lemma 09XH).* $A\to A'$ is of finite presentation, in particular of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] (1). Let $B'\subseteq A'$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $A'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-fibre-part-localization] applied to $A\to A'$, $A'/IA'=C_1\times C$ and $\varepsilon$ of step 1, there are an idempotent $\varepsilon'\in B'/IB'$ and $b\in B'$ such that: $B'/IB'\to\bar A'$ maps $\varepsilon'$ to $\varepsilon$; the induced map $\varepsilon'(B'/IB')\to\varepsilon\bar A'=C_1$ is an isomorphism, so with step 1, $(B'/IB')_{\varepsilon'}\cong\varepsilon'(B'/IB')\cong A/I$, as $A$-algebras (for an idempotent $\eta$ of a ring $R$, $R_\eta\cong\eta R=R/(1-\eta)R$); $b$ maps to $\varepsilon'$ in $B'/IB'$; and $B'_b\to A'_b$ is an isomorphism. (Stacks: equation (dec-mod-I) and 'we may find $b\in B'$ that lifts $(1,0)$ such that $B'_b\to A'_b$ is an isomorphism'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), third paragraph ('Let $B'$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $A'$. By Lemma 09XH ...')

proof.text: *A finite subalgebra $B''$ (Stacks' fourth paragraph, details written out).* (a) Since $b\mapsto\varepsilon'$ is idempotent, $b^2-b\in IB'$: write $b^2-b=\sum_{k=1}^si_k\gamma_k$ with $i_k\in I$, $\gamma_k\in B'$. (b) $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra (step 2), hence so is $A'_b=A'[1/b]$ (add the generator $1/b$), hence so is $B'_b\cong A'_b$ (step 2); choose generators and write them with a common denominator as $\beta_1/b^n,\dots,\beta_t/b^n$ with $\beta_k\in B'$. (c) Let $B''\subseteq B'$ be the $A$-subalgebra generated by $b,\beta_1,\dots,\beta_t,\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_s$. Its generators are integral over $A$, so $A\to B''$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators]. (d) $B''_b\to B'_b$ is injective (if $\beta/b^m\mapsto0$ then $b^N\beta=0$ in $B'$, hence in $B''\subseteq B'$) and surjective (its image is an $A$-subalgebra containing the generators $\beta_k/b^n$), so it is an isomorphism. (e) The image $\varepsilon''$ of $b$ in $B''/IB''$ is idempotent by (a), giving $B''/IB''=B_1\times B_2$ with $B_1=\varepsilon''(B''/IB'')$, $B_2=(1-\varepsilon'')(B''/IB'')$, and $b\mapsto(1,0)$. Localization commutes with quotients, so $B_1\cong(B''/IB'')_{\varepsilon''}=B''_b/IB''_b\cong B'_b/IB'_b=(B'/IB')_{\varepsilon'}\cong A/I$ (by (d) and step 2), all maps being $A$-algebra maps. The composite $A/I\to B_1\cong A/I$ is an $A$-algebra endomorphism of $A/I$, hence the identity; so the structure map $A/I\to B_1$ is an isomorphism, in particular surjective ('we see that $C''_1=A/I$!').

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), fourth paragraph ('Choose a finite $A$-subalgebra $B''\subset B'$ containing $b$ ... $B''_b\to B'_b$ is surjective as well as injective, hence an isomorphism. In particular, we see that $C''_1=A/I$!')

proof.text: *Gabber's polynomial (Lemma 0EM0).* $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A$ (hypothesis (a)), $A\to B''$ is finite and $B''/IB''=B_1\times B_2$ with $A/I\to B_1$ surjective and $b\mapsto(1,0)$ (step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-pair-finite-gabber-polynomial] there are $n\ge1$ and a monic $f\in A[T]$ with $f(b)=0$ in $B''$, hence in $B'$, and $f\equiv(T-1)T^n$ modulo $I$, i.e. $f=T^n(T-1)+a_nT^n+\dots+a_1T+a_0$ with $a_0,\dots,a_n\in I$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), fourth paragraph ('By Lemma 0EM0 we can find an $f(T)\in A[T]$ of the form ... such that $f(b)=0$')

proof.text: *The root and the idempotent of $A[T]/(f)$.* By hypothesis (b) $f$ has a root $\alpha\in1+I$. Every element of $1+I$ is a unit of $A$ (if $1+i$ were not a unit it would lie in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$; as $i\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ by (a), $1\in\mathfrak m$). Division by the monic $T-\alpha$ gives $f=(T-\alpha)g$ with $g\in A[T]$ monic of degree $n$ (the remainder is $f(\alpha)=0$). Modulo $I$: $T^n(T-1)=(T-1)\bar g$ in $(A/I)[T]$, and $T-1$ is monic, hence a nonzerodivisor, so $\bar g=T^n$. Hence $g(\alpha)\equiv\bar g(1)=1$ modulo $I$, so $g(\alpha)$ is a unit; put $u=g(\alpha)^{-1}\in A$. Division of $g$ by $T-\alpha$ gives $g=g(\alpha)+(T-\alpha)q$ with $q\in A[T]$, so $ug-uq(T-\alpha)=1$. Put $E=ug\in A[T]$. Then $E-1=uq(T-\alpha)$, so $E^2-E=E(E-1)=u^2q\,g(T-\alpha)=u^2qf\in(f)$, and $(T-\alpha)E=uf\in(f)$. ($E$ is the idempotent of the decomposition $A[T]/(f)=A[T]/(T-\alpha)\times A[T]/(g)$ of Stacks.) Let $e=E(b)\in B'$. Since $f(b)=0$ (step 4): $e^2=e$ and $(b-\alpha)e=0$, i.e. $be=\alpha e$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), last paragraph ('By (5) we deduce there is a root $a\in1+I$ of $f$. This produces a product decomposition $A[T]/(f)=A[T]/(T-a)\times D$'), written out

proof.text: *$e$ lifts $\varepsilon'$.* In $(A/I)[T]$, $\bar E=\bar u\,\bar g=T^n$, since $\bar u=\overline{g(\alpha)}^{-1}=1$ (step 5). The image of $b$ in $B'/IB'$ is $\varepsilon'$ (step 2), so the image of $e=E(b)$ is $\bar E(\varepsilon')=\varepsilon'^n=\varepsilon'$, as $n\ge1$ and $\varepsilon'$ is idempotent. Consequently the image of $e$ in $\bar A'$ is the image of $\varepsilon'$, which is $\varepsilon$ (step 2). (Stacks: 'compatible with the splitting (dec-mod-I) of $B'/IB'$'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), last paragraph ('compatible with the splitting (\ref{equation-dec-mod-I}) of $B'/IB'$')

proof.text: *$A'_e$ is integral over $A$ (Stacks: 'since $b$ is a unit in $B'_1$ (details omitted), we will have $B'_1\cong A'_1$').* In $B'_e$ and in $A'_e$ we have $e/1=1$, so $b/1=\alpha/1$ by step 5, a unit since $\alpha$ is a unit of $A$. Hence, by the universal property of localization, the localization maps give $B'_e\cong(B'_b)_{e}$ and $A'_e\cong(A'_b)_{e}$ (both are the localization at the multiplicative set generated by $b$ and $e$). The isomorphism $B'_b\cong A'_b$ of step 2 sends $e/1$ to $e/1$, so it induces $(B'_b)_e\cong(A'_b)_e$; hence the map $B'_e\to A'_e$ induced by $B'\subseteq A'$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras. As $e$ is idempotent, $B'_e\cong B'/(1-e)B'$ is a quotient of $B'$, which is integral over $A$; so $B'_e$, and with it $A'_e$, is integral over $A$. (This is the decomposition $A'=eA'\times(1-e)A'\cong A'_e\times A'_{1-e}$ of (GCHP-want) with $A'_1=A'_e$ integral over $A$.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5)$\Rightarrow$(2), third paragraph ('then the induced decomposition $A'=A'_1\times A'_2$ will give the desired (GCHP-want): indeed, since $b$ is a unit in $B'_1$ (details omitted), we will have $B'_1\cong A'_1$')

proof.text: The section takes the lifted idempotent to 1, so it extends to the localization. Localization commutes with quotient; the reduced idempotent cuts out A/I, so the induced quotient structure map is bijective. These facts provide rho and its compatibility on B, without identifying the localization with A.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09XI, proof of (5) implies (2), construction of the integral first factor only; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XI on 2026-10-12.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_gabber_integral_section_factor
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥)
    (hroots : ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (a : Fin (n + 1) → A),
      (∀ j, a j ∈ I) → ∀ (f : A[X]), f.Monic →
        f = X ^ n * (X - 1) + ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), C (a j) * X ^ (j : ℕ) →
          ∃ α : A, α - 1 ∈ I ∧ f.IsRoot α)
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Etale A B] (σ : B →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I) :
    ∃ e : B, IsIdempotentElem e ∧
      (algebraMap A (Localization.Away e)).IsIntegral ∧
      Function.Bijective
        (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away e)) I)
          (algebraMap A (Localization.Away e)) Ideal.le_comap_map) ∧
      ∃ ρ : Localization.Away e →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I,
        ∀ x : B, ρ (algebraMap B (Localization.Away e) x) = σ x
